requirements.quote: Postgres archives WAL continuously through WAL-G; the time since the last archived WAL is below 5 minutes in steady state and is exposed as a metric [type:api]
A nightly base backup runs, is verified with `wal-g backup-list`, and the retention policy keeps 14 daily base backups plus WAL for 14 days of PITR, and 8 weekly backups, configurable [type:api]
Backups are encrypted client-side; restoring without the key fails; the key is not stored on the database host disk unprotected and its custody is documented [type:manual]
Backup storage and the second MinIO or bucket location are in India regions only; Terraform or config validation rejects non-India endpoints [type:unit]
MinIO replication copies new objects to the second India location within 24 hours (nightly replicate) with object versioning and delete protection, verified by a test object [type:api]

The restore drill restores the latest backup plus WAL to a specified timestamp into an isolated container, completes verification (`amcheck`, row-count manifest, RLS enabled on every tenant table, cross-tenant query returns zero rows) and writes a JSON report [type:api]
Measured RPO is at most 15 minutes and measured RTO for the seeded dataset is recorded each drill and compared with the 4-hour target; a breach opens an alert [type:api]
The weekly drill runs automatically against staging and the monthly drill is signed off by a human recorded in `infra/runbooks/drills/` with date, duration and findings [type:manual]
requirements.evidence: .github/workflows/restore-drill.yml (weekly schedule); monthly sign-off files in infra/runbooks/drills/ (human)

requirements.quote: A failed backup, stale WAL or failed drill triggers an alert through the monitoring stack in #102 within 10 minutes [type:api]
requirements.why: Alert routing and the monitoring stack are #102 (open, listed out of scope in #101). This change delivers the signals: the four metrics, a system.backup.health job that runs every minute and logs/errors on failed backup, stale WAL (>5 min) or failed/RTO-breaching drill, and documents the alert thresholds in the runbook for #102 to wire.

requirements.quote: Restoring never overwrites production in place without the explicit `--i-understand` flag and a fresh target volume; the script refuses otherwise [type:unit]
Crypto-erase interplay is documented and tested: after a workspace deletion job plus the key-backup retention window, the workspace DEK cannot be recovered from backups [type:manual]
The runbook describes the DR scenario of losing the VPS: provision from Terraform, restore from WAL-G, point DNS, expected duration, and has been rehearsed at least once before launch [type:manual]
requirements.evidence: Runbook is delivered here; the rehearsal needs the real VPS (#108) and storage credentials (#116) and is recorded in infra/runbooks/drills/ before launch

requirements.quote: A backup that has never been restored is not a backup, so the drill runs weekly in CI-like automation and monthly with a human sign-off.
requirements.evidence: .github/workflows/restore-drill.yml weekly job; monthly sign-off by a human

requirements.quote: backups contain privileged client data: encryption in transit and at rest, least-privilege storage credentials (write-only for the archiver, separate read credentials for restore), no public buckets, access logged.

decisions.choice: Job is `system.backup.health` in packages/core/src/jobs/definitions/, not `ops.backup.health` in apps/worker/src/jobs/
decisions.justification: Non-system job names must require workspaceId (packages/core/src/jobs/define.ts:104-106); every definition lives in core and is registered in registry.ts (precedent audit-retention.ts:78)

decisions.choice: No new workspace dependency: core already depends on @causedeck/storage and @causedeck/observability
Scripts publish status JSON to an ops bucket in MinIO; the worker job reads it, so the worker needs no docker or Postgres-archiver access
decisions.justification: Worker has storage access already; keeps the health job testable with an injected reader

decisions.choice: Weekly retention via `wal-g backup-mark` permanent on Sunday backups, expired after 8 weeks, plus `wal-g delete retain FULL 14`
decisions.justification: WAL-G has no native daily/weekly tiers; permanent marking keeps a base backup and its WAL until unmarked

decisions.choice: Full backup→PITR integration test runs only in CI against local MinIO; local validate uses static/unit tests
decisions.justification: CLAUDE.md: never run Docker-heavy/e2e locally on the shared host; precedent infra/docker/test/compose-smoke.sh

decisions.choice: Encryption uses WAL-G libsodium with the key file on a root-owned 0600 tmpfs/secret path, custody copies off host
decisions.justification: Issue requirement R3 allows libsodium or GPG; key not stored unprotected on the DB host disk
